Marathon Petroleum has gained 7.8% over two weeks and inched up 0.3% today, riding a sharp rally since late August. The core driver is the refining environment: U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity while diesel and heating oil inventories sit near historic lows (104 million barrels), pushing diesel prices to record highs and boosting margins for refiners like Marathon. Oil prices have also climbed—U.S. crude at $91.48—as geopolitical tensions escalate, with the Ukraine war damaging Russian refineries and new Iran sanctions cutting off another major global supply source.

The broader backdrop amplifies this. Diesel shortages are feeding inflation concerns and tightening refining capacity globally just as demand remains strong, which typically translates to wider profit margins for U.S. refiners who can run at full tilt. The tightness in refined products rather than crude oil itself is the key tailwind here.
